summary: Milnacipran is a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI) approved for the management of fibromyalgia (it is not approved as an antidepressant in the US). It relieves fibromyalgia pain by enhancing descending pain-inhibitory pathways. It carries the class boxed warning for increased suicidality in children, adolescents and young adults, and can raise blood pressure and heart rate.

moa: Milnacipran inhibits the reuptake of both serotonin and norepinephrine, with relatively greater potency for norepinephrine, increasing their availability in the central nervous system. In fibromyalgia this is thought to strengthen descending inhibitory pain pathways and reduce central pain sensitisation. It has little affinity for muscarinic, histaminergic, or adrenergic receptors.

absolute: Concurrent or recent (within 14 days) monoamine oxidase inhibitor use
relative: History of seizures or mania/bipolar disorder

preg: Use only if the potential benefit justifies the risk. Use in the third trimester may cause neonatal complications (respiratory distress, feeding difficulty, jitteriness) requiring monitoring. Discuss individualized risk.
lact: Limited data on excretion into human milk. Use with caution and monitor the breastfed infant for irritability, poor feeding, or sedation.
renal: Reduce the maintenance dose to 25 mg twice daily in severe renal impairment (CrCl 5-29 mL/min), with possible increase to 50 mg twice daily as tolerated. Not recommended in end-stage renal disease.
hepatic: Use with caution; not recommended in patients with chronic liver disease or substantial alcohol use due to risk of hepatotoxicity. Monitor liver function if used.

missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember unless it is close to the next dose, in which case skip it - do not double up. If you miss several doses, contact your prescriber rather than restarting at the full dose, and never stop abruptly.
overdose: Reported overdose effects include increased blood pressure, nausea/vomiting, somnolence, tachycardia, and in serotonergic combinations serotonin syndrome. There is no specific antidote; provide supportive care with cardiovascular and CNS monitoring. Because of high protein binding and large volume of distribution, dialysis is unlikely to help.
